name.text: Calculating exact Values of Trigonometric Ratios for Negative Angles

questiontext.text:
Without using a calculator, find the exact value of \( \sin({@ang1@}^\circ) + \cos({@ang2@}^\circ). \)

(a) Find \(\sin({@ang1@}^\circ) = \) [[input:ans1]] [[validation:ans1]] [[feedback:prt1]]

(b) Find \(\cos({@ang2@}^\circ) = \) [[input:ans2]] [[validation:ans2]] [[feedback:prt2]]

(c) Hence find \(\sin({@ang1@}^\circ) + \cos({@ang2@}^\circ)\), as simply as possible.

\(\sin({@ang1@}^\circ) + \cos({@ang2@}^\circ) = \) [[input:ans3]] [[validation:ans3]] [[feedback:prt3]]

Give each answer in exact form: for example, type sqrt(3)/2 for \(\dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\).

generalfeedback.text:
Worked Solution

(a) Finding \(\sin({@ang1@}^\circ)\)

Step 1: rewrite with a positive angle. Since \(\sin(-\theta) = -\sin\theta\),

\[ \sin({@ang1@}^\circ) = -\sin({@t1@}^\circ). \]

Step 2: find the quadrant and the reference angle. \({@t1@}^\circ\) lies in Quadrant {@qn1@}, so its reference angle (the acute angle between the terminal side and the \(x\)-axis) is [[if test="is(q1=1)"]]\(\alpha = {@t1@}^\circ\) itself[[/if]][[if test="is(q1=2)"]]\(\alpha = 180^\circ - {@t1@}^\circ = {@ref1@}^\circ\)[[/if]][[if test="is(q1=3)"]]\(\alpha = {@t1@}^\circ - 180^\circ = {@ref1@}^\circ\)[[/if]][[if test="is(q1=4)"]]\(\alpha = 360^\circ - {@t1@}^\circ = {@ref1@}^\circ\)[[/if]].

Step 3: find \(\sin({@t1@}^\circ)\). From the special triangles, \(\sin {@ref1@}^\circ = {@sref1@}\). In Quadrant {@qn1@} the sine (the \(y\)-coordinate) is [[if test="is(q1<3)"]]positive[[else]]negative[[/if]], so

\[ \sin({@t1@}^\circ) = {@s1@}. \]

Step 4: apply the minus sign from Step 1.

\[ \sin({@ang1@}^\circ) = -\left({@s1@}\right) = {@sin_ans@}. \]

In the diagram, turning clockwise through \({@-ang1@}^\circ\) ends at \(P\) [[if test="is(sin_ans>0)"]]above[[else]]below[[/if]] the \(x\)-axis, so the \(y\)-coordinate of \(P\) (green) is [[if test="is(sin_ans>0)"]]positive[[else]]negative[[/if]], as found.

(b) Finding \(\cos({@ang2@}^\circ)\)

Step 1: rewrite with a positive angle. Since \(\cos(-\theta) = \cos\theta\),

\[ \cos({@ang2@}^\circ) = \cos({@t2@}^\circ). \]

Step 2: find the quadrant and the reference angle. \({@t2@}^\circ\) lies in Quadrant {@qn2@}, so its reference angle (the acute angle between the terminal side and the \(x\)-axis) is [[if test="is(q2=1)"]]\(\alpha = {@t2@}^\circ\) itself[[/if]][[if test="is(q2=2)"]]\(\alpha = 180^\circ - {@t2@}^\circ = {@ref2@}^\circ\)[[/if]][[if test="is(q2=3)"]]\(\alpha = {@t2@}^\circ - 180^\circ = {@ref2@}^\circ\)[[/if]][[if test="is(q2=4)"]]\(\alpha = 360^\circ - {@t2@}^\circ = {@ref2@}^\circ\)[[/if]].

Step 3: find \(\cos({@t2@}^\circ)\). From the special triangles, \(\cos {@ref2@}^\circ = {@cref2@}\). In Quadrant {@qn2@} the cosine (the \(x\)-coordinate) is [[if test="is(q2=1 or q2=4)"]]positive[[else]]negative[[/if]], so

\[ \cos({@ang2@}^\circ) = \cos({@t2@}^\circ) = {@cos_ans@}. \]

In the diagram, \(P\) is to the [[if test="is(cos_ans>0)"]]right[[else]]left[[/if]] of the \(y\)-axis, so its \(x\)-coordinate (blue) is [[if test="is(cos_ans>0)"]]positive[[else]]negative[[/if]].

(c) Adding the two values

\[ \sin({@ang1@}^\circ) + \cos({@ang2@}^\circ) = {@sin_ans@} + \left({@cos_ans@}\right). \]

The two values are like terms, so they can be added directly:

\[ \sin({@ang1@}^\circ) + \cos({@ang2@}^\circ) = {@ta@}. \]
